entries.name: Fred Shuttlesworth

expected.sentence:
90 days at hard labor, plus 48 days in default of the fine and costs. Actual time served not documented (conviction reversed).

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted under Birmingham's parade ordinance; the conviction was reversed by the Supreme Court in 1969.

Charges as recorded: Parading without a permit — for helping lead a Good Friday civil-rights march of 52 people without a permit, alongside Martin Luther King Jr. and Ralph Abernathy (Shuttlesworth v. City of Birmingham, 394 U.S. 147).

entries.rationale: Deborah A. Roy, Journal of Supreme Court History 38(3), printed page 418 (PDF 140), explicitly dates bond release April 13, 1963; footnote 56 cites Diane McWhorter, Carry Me Home, page 347. Original page visually checked. Ninety-day sentence is not ninety days actually served. Preserve sentence and biography.

entries.name: James Forman

expected.charges: Breach of peace; parading without a permit (civil rights organizing)
expected.convicted: Multiple short convictions across the 1961–1965 SNCC organizing campaigns

entries.rationale: This umbrella record describes multiple short sentences, not uninterrupted 1961-1965 custody. FBI Albany report PDF pages 18 and 22-24 documents Forman freely leading demonstrations on August 1, 1962 before a new arrest, disproving the continuous interval. Clear unsupported continuous endpoints and derived 1308-day total.
